description: Brian Cox investigates the nature and measurement of time before turning outward to the solar system, exploring the Sun, planetary formation, atmospheres, geology and the conditions that make worlds capable of supporting life.

s01e00.description: Brian Cox investigates what time actually is, from ancient calendars and atomic measurement to relativity, the beginning of the universe and the possibility that our sense of time is an illusion.

s01e01.description: Brian explores the Sun as the powerhouse of the solar system and follows the effects of its energy and solar wind from Earth to other worlds.

s01e02.description: Brian examines how order emerged from the solar system’s chaotic beginnings, using phenomena on Earth and Saturn’s rings to reveal the governing physics.

s01e03.description: Brian explores how thin envelopes of gas create some of the solar system’s most extraordinary sights and make worlds such as Earth habitable.

s01e04.description: Brian examines how a world’s size and geological history can determine whether it remains active and potentially hospitable to life.

s01e05.description: Brian follows the search for water across the solar system and explains why finding it is central to the search for extraterrestrial life.
